B also invents a small scene ('kids in the car') but holds the urgency more steadily and adds fewer claims that aren't on the sheet. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both emails are complete and use the facts correctly, including the derived $18,600 and 8-meals-per-dollar figures. B adds things not on the fact sheet: that the match 'will not be extended', the parents 'sent home to bare cupboards' scene, and the claim that winter need is greatest. B's 'I can't promise we'll never run short' also slightly softens the push. A stays strong and urgent with only small embellishments ('kids in the car'), so it is cleaner and more faithful to the facts.
